fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is only a technical amendment to aeronautical study factors with a purely internal agency directive, so no outside party is involved. However, subsection (b) requires the FAA Administrator to initiate a rulemaking, and under the definition a required rulemaking counts as participation because it brings in public notice and comment.
fable.s: the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration shall initiate a rulemaking to implement the amendments made by subsection (a).

opus.w: Subsection (b) requires the FAA Administrator to start a rulemaking. Under the definition, requiring rulemaking counts as participation, because rulemaking includes notice and public comment. It is tempting to read the whole section as a technical amendment adding space launch and reentry to the factors in 49 U.S.C. 44718(b)(1). That reading misses the rulemaking mandate.
opus.s: Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration shall initiate a rulemaking to implement the amendments made by subsection (a).

qwen_chat.w: The section explicitly requires the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to initiate a rulemaking. According to the definition, requiring rulemaking is a form of participation because it typically involves public comment periods and other procedures that allow outside parties to influence federal decisions. Therefore, this section mandates participation.
qwen_chat.s: (b) Rulemaking.—Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration shall initiate a rulemaking to implement the amendments made by subsection (a).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "rulemaking" is a generic administrative process that doesn't necessarily involve public participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "requiring rulemaking" is a form of participation because federal rulemaking under the Administrative Procedure Act generally requires public notice and comment periods, allowing the public to participate in the decision-making process.
